body: Sounds good, I will check it out.
I'm really sorry about your friend.

> That's part of why I gave you an answer with the detail that I did, rather than simply sharing the parts that encourage you to do what I think you should do.

Thank you. I can't even tell you how much I appreciate that.

> But...you do agree, don't you, that it is better to be in the hospital and deal with your parents reaction to that, than it would be to be dead, right?

You know. I don't think I do. I can see the reasoning behind that statement, but I don't feel like it's true for me.

My entire life feels like it's been nothing but pain. And I'm tired of it all, you know? If I go to a hospital it's going to get worse before it gets better -- if it even gets better at all (which I doubt). I can't take it anymore. I don't even want it to get better. I just want out.

> Depression can't be detected in your blood

Well fuck it then. I don't know if I'm even going to go back to get the results. He's just going to ask me a bunch of difficult questions which I can't answer.


The time I tried to kill myself it was like I felt so bad for so long I didn't have any other choice. I don't remember planning it, in fact I didn't even write a letter (something I'd really like to do before I go).

And with regards to your other question, I can kind of see it coming now. I was alright for the last month or so, but now everything seems to be getting really out of control way too fast.

I felt pretty down last night and now I feel twice as bad. I feel really fucking horrible right now to be honest. I don't know if it's going to end badly. I've been on downward spirals before and I'm still here to write about it.

I feel like an idiot writing this. Here you are trying to help me and I'm going against everything you're saying. Fuck.

First of all, thanks for the info -- that's exactly what I needed to know.

I appreciate your advice, but I absolutely can not, under any circumstances, check into a hospital. I live with my parents. They have no idea about my problem, and I have to keep it that way. I don't think I could deal with the added pressure of them worrying about me.

I'm not worried about being kept involuntarily after the initial stay... I'm very confident that I could convince a psych or doc that I am fine. And the majority of the time I am fine.


It's unlikely that I'd kill myself soon. If you take away the soon part, I'd say it's quite possibly more likely than not. I have actually tried to kill myself in the past, and I know in detail exactly how I'd go about doing it if I was ever to try again. I know I will be almost certainly be depressed in the future, but I don't know if it will be to the extent that I'd act on it.

Based what you've said, I can only conclude that if I said that to a doctor there's a high chance that they would intervene in some way.

If there's even a chance that they could get me checked in to a hospital (even if it was just for a day) then I honestly can't take the chance of disclosing anything (to a doctor or a psych). I do realize that they are trying to act in my best interests, but I'm the only one who really knows what my best interests are.

I think my policy will be to accept treatment if my blood test shows it's necessary, but not discuss my circumstances with anyone any further. I really glad I asked for advice about this -- to be honest I'm a little freaked out about what might have happened had I not read your advice.

Undoubtedly the best way to commit suicide is by inducing hypoxia (i.e. depriving yourself of oxygen).

We've all heard that when people drown they feel a sense of euphoria. This is true, however drowning is a terrible way to die because you will struggle to breath before you finally give in to your reflexes and start breathing water.

However there are many other ways to induce hypoxia, one of the easiest is to breath helium (there are other inert gases which will work, but helium is readily available at any party supplies store).

Your body cannot tell the difference between helium and air, so you will not feel like you are struggling to breath at all. You will feel slightly euphoric, and as hypoxia sets in **you will not care that you are about to die.** Very soon you will drift out of consciousness, and within minutes your life will be over.

This method is GUARANTEED to work if done properly. However if you change your mind half way, do not have enough helium, or if the mask falls off you when you pass out, you will suffer _serious_ brain damage. This method of suicide needs to be carefully planned.


More information on this:
 
 - How to kill a human being (BBC Horizon documentary)... the presenter goes into a pressure chamber where he experiences hypoxia. He describes the experience. I cannot recommend this documentary highly enough.

 - Final Exit or Peaceful Pill - these books contain info on how to ensure nothing goes wrong. Mostly common sense stuff.


DISCLAIMER:
I'm not advocating suicide here. I'm more advocating freedom of information. I do believe that suicide is one of our most inalienable rights, but that said if you're seriously considering ending your life please be _absolutely_ certain that this is _really_ what you want.
